title: Inventory Value for a date before a rename shows the old part number
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a tracked part, part A, for this test on an earlier day, date A, with 4 in its bin at a cost of $10.00, so the Inventory Value report saved a figure for it on date A.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Click the part A row.
  2. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  3. Click Save.
  4. Click Reports in the top bar.
  5. Click Inventory Value.
  6. Pick the test location only in the Location filter.
  7. Set the as-of date to date A.
  8. Type part A's old part number in the report's Search box.
  9. Set the as-of date to today.
  10. Replace the search text with the new number.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 2:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 3:

  • The window closes and part A's row shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The Reports page opens.

Step 5:

  • The Inventory Value report opens.

Step 6:

  • The report shows the test location only.

Step 7:

  • The report shows date A.

Step 8:

  • Part A is listed for date A under its old number, with Qty 4.00, Unit Cost $10.00 and Total Cost $40.00 (4 × $10.00).

Step 9:

  • For today no row is listed under the old number, because today's report shows the new number.

Step 10:

  • For today part A is listed under the new number, with Qty 4.00 and Total Cost $40.00.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • Story 13, context note: “Context note: S13-R19 matters because those records hold their own copy of the number and find the part by it later. Records already completed, such as received purchase order lines, completed returns and past work orders and invoices, keep the number they were written with. The Inventory list, Part History, Parts Velocity and today's Inventory Value show the new number. Inventory Value run for a date before the rename shows the number as it was on that date.”
  • S13-R18: “Saving a changed number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every line that holds it. Its Part Library entry is renamed with it, and its core takes the same number. No new Part Library entry is created.”
  • Feature Overview, Accounting: “The Inventory Value report run for a past date shows each part as it was on that date. Turning tracking off today does not change an earlier date's figures.”
